genius.headline: UW-Madison physicist Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize in physics for IceCube neutrino work
genius.summary: On October 6, Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physics. He has been on the University of Wisconsin-Madison faculty since 1972 and is principal investigator of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. According to the Nobel committee, his work was instrumental to building IceCube, which uses Antarctic ice as a neutrino detector and glimpsed the first high-energy neutrinos from faraway galaxies. Halzen is 82 and is the sixth physicist connected to UW-Madison to win a Nobel.

quote.text: UW-Madison professor Francis Halzen has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in physics for his work on the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from space.

facepalm.headline: South Portland has 19,000 ballots reprinted after bond total is listed as $105 million, not $150 million
facepalm.summary: South Portland, Maine, is having 19,000 municipal ballots reprinted after a public safety bond question for a new police and fire station listed the total of principal and estimated interest as $105,398,500 instead of $150,398,500. The city said its printer transposed a number. Early voting had already started; ballots already cast will count, and voters can ask for a new ballot if they want to change their vote.

quote.text: While we submitted the correct total of $150,398,500, they mistakenly transposed a number and listed $105,398,500 on the ballot
